entries.title: II Kings 23:3
segments:
Stood to the covenant; accepted it and bound themselves to fulfil it. 
 
No repentance is genuine which does not lead to external reformation; and no reformation is accepted of God, but such as springs from the heart, and is persevered in to the end.

entries.title: II Kings 23:4
segments:
The grove; the wooden statue of Astarte. 
 
  Fields of Kidron; on the east side of Jerusalem, through which ran the brook of that name.
Unto Bethel; which, as the chief seat of idolatry under the Israelitish kings, he purposed to defile in every way.  See

entries.title: II Kings 23:6
segments: The grove; see note to

. 
 
Things which have been used as instruments, and which operate as incentives to evil, should be effectually removed, and either destroyed or so treated that their evil influence.

entries.title: II Kings 23:8
segments:
vv 8-9. 
 
  All the priests--came not up to the altar; these were Levitical priests who had been set apart to burn incense on the high places. Josiah, after he had taken away their unlawful office, would not allow them to minister any more at God's altar in Jerusalem, but granted them their regular portion which fell to them as priests forbidden to officiate.  Compare
.  Some suppose that they were the same as the idolatrous priests mentioned

.  But there another word is used in the original, which is not elsewhere applied to Levitical priests. 
 
  Geba; in the north part of Judea. 
 
  Beer-sheba; in the south part of Judea.

entries.title: II Kings 23:10
segments: The valley of the children of Hinnom; a deep valley on the south-east side of Jerusalem, in which idolaters made their children pass through fire in honor of their idol gods.

entries.title: II Kings 23:12
segments: The altars--of Ahaz; which had been erected to idols.

entries.title: II Kings 23:13
segments:
Mount of corruption; supposed to be the mount of Olives. 
 
  Ashtoreth--Chemosh--Milcom; idol gods.

entries.title: II Kings 23:15
segments: The altar that was at Beth-el; consecrated to the worship of the golden calf set up by Jeroboam the son of Nebat,

.  The kingdom of Israel no longer existed, but many of the Israelites remained in their own country.  Josiah found himself able to go through the cities of Samaria and destroy their idolatrous places without molestation from the distant Assyrian monarchs, who were already falling before the rising Chaldean empire.

entries.title: II Kings 23:16
segments: The man of God;
Though the fulfilment of divine declarations may be long delayed, and many may conclude that they will never be accomplished, not one jot or tittle of them will fail to come to pass.

entries.title: II Kings 23:17
segments: Title; or, monument.

entries.title: II Kings 23:22
segments: Such a passover; with such solemnity, and in such strict accordance with the law of Moses, a copy of which had recently been found in the temple.

entries.title: II Kings 23:25
segments: No penitence on the part of individuals, and no external reformation of those over whom htey have influence, can save guilty nations who have sinned away ther day of grace, from meeting the retribution which they deserve.

entries.title: II Kings 23:29
segments:
Megiddo; near the Kishon, and on the border of the great plain of Esdraelon.  The highway from Egypt to Assyria led by this place. 
 
Though pious men may, through their own fault or the wickedness of others, come to an untimely and violent death, it will be well with them at last.

entries.title: II Kings 23:33
segments: Put him in bands at Riblah; after he had first deposed him from his kingly office in Jerusalem.
The district of Hamath lay on the northern border of Palestine, and through it the armies of Egypt on the one side, and Assyria and Babylon on the other, passed in their wars with each other.
